properties.name: An import says which properties it removed or changed on records that already existed, and keeps the ones left out only when the call asks it to merge
properties.statement:
import_graph keeps whole-node semantics by default, so an export→import round trip still reproduces a design and a document can still remove a property. Its reply counts, per property, what it removed or changed on nodes that already existed and names a few (for example properties_dropped: {checksum: 454, …}), so a partial document can never silently wipe data. When the call asks for merge, a partial node's properties are merged into the existing node, as create_node and create_nodes do. The served description stops promising that a partial node is refused (today only a missing REQUIRED property is, and an Artifact requires only `name`), and the adopt skill sends bulk edits of existing records to create_nodes, which merges, instead of saying there is no incremental equivalent.
WHY (root cause, measured 2026-10-21 on the published 0.89.0 binary and origin/main f3e85e7cd): hxm_program updated 454 artifacts with {name, location} through import_graph; checksum, checksum_basis and status were dropped on all 454 and the reply said only nodes_written: 454. Reproduced on a throwaway store: checksum, checksum_basis, status and description lost, artifact_type reset from config to code and reported under `materialized` as if a default were filled; create_nodes with the same partial properties kept everything. Causes: import writes through a whole-node replace on purpose (export.rs:581 → graph.rs:1009-1022); the promised partial-node refusal checks only required properties (exchange.rs:447-448); the reply counts only what it added (export.rs:582-589); and, outside the component, the adopt skill (SKILL.md:142-153) steers bulk work to import_graph. The same reply gap sits under fact:root-cause-the-record-moved-hint-recommended-an-import-that-reverted-three-newer-live-edits-2026-09-23.
